code generation, debugging, reviews and memory use must respect this constraint even
if an upstream generic prompt suggests an ensemble. The host audits the actual

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

Diagnosis targets a two-layer, pre-norm BERT4Rec: scaled item embeddings plus absolute position embeddings pass through dropout, bidirectional Transformer layers, and final normalization. Histories are left padded, truncated to `maxlen−1`, and followed by a reserved MASK. Its final-slot feature supplies the user representation for candidate scoring; PAD holes are excluded from attention keys.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` accesses the actual network through `view.model`, embeddings through `view.item_emb`, training histories, and `log2feats`/`predict_score`. Loader batches contain `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with matching B×L tensors.

Serving verification reloads the current category’s exported checkpoint, checks exact state identity, and compares explicit encoder features, ModelView outputs, internal scoring, exported prediction, and batched versus individual scoring. Short, full, and truncated histories must all be covered.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding alignment:** mapped mean pairwise cosine over up to 2,048 real-item embeddings. Near 1 indicates strong alignment; 0.5 means approximately zero mean cosine, without establishing capacity or quality.
- **Masked-target separation:** up to ten batches yield mean/p10 positive-minus-negative margins, negative-win rate, and margins below 0.5. Larger margins and fewer negative wins indicate stronger in-sample separation. Sampler checks enforce reserved tokens and MASK-only supervised positions.
- **History sensitivity:** up to 64 seeded training users contribute one eligible prefix and 100 fixed candidates. Measurements include target score/rank, reciprocal rank, diagnostic hit@10, top-10 overlap, and complete ranking agreement. Paired changes receive 500-bootstrap user intervals; sensitivity itself is not inherently good or bad.

# Perturbation & Tests

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

Diagnosis targets a two-layer, pre-norm BERT4Rec: scaled item embeddings plus absolute position embeddings pass through dropout, bidirectional Transformer layers, and final normalization. Histories are left padded, truncated to `maxlen−1`, and followed by a reserved MASK. Its final-slot feature supplies the user representation for candidate scoring; PAD holes are excluded from attention keys.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` accesses the actual network through `view.model`, embeddings through `view.item_emb`, training histories, and `log2feats`/`predict_score`. Loader batches contain `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with matching B×L tensors.

Serving verification reloads the current category’s exported checkpoint, checks exact state identity, and compares explicit encoder features, ModelView outputs, internal scoring, exported prediction, and batched versus individual scoring. Short, full, and truncated histories must all be covered.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding alignment:** mapped mean pairwise cosine over up to 2,048 real-item embeddings. Near 1 indicates strong alignment; 0.5 means approximately zero mean cosine, without establishing capacity or quality.
- **Masked-target separation:** up to ten batches yield mean/p10 positive-minus-negative margins, negative-win rate, and margins below 0.5. Larger margins and fewer negative wins indicate stronger in-sample separation. Sampler checks enforce reserved tokens and MASK-only supervised positions.
- **History sensitivity:** up to 64 seeded training users contribute one eligible prefix and 100 fixed candidates. Measurements include target score/rank, reciprocal rank, diagnostic hit@10, top-10 overlap, and complete ranking agreement. Paired changes receive 500-bootstrap user intervals; sensitivity itself is not inherently good or bad.

# Perturbation & Tests

Delete matched counts of recent or older items into PAD holes, preserving positions, or swap the final two items. Sensitivity requires passing sampler and serving checks.

A 30-second residual-patching pilot replaces the latest item using two frequency/recency-matched donor rules. Clean/corrupted activations are patched before attention layers. Exploration locks sites/signs; disjoint confirmation users receive sign tests. Identity, structural-zero, MASK-restoration, norm-matched random, and unrelated-donor controls accompany margin/ranking effects.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`, including status, counts, availability, parity, sensitivity, patching records, controls, intervals, and elapsed time. Execution restores model mode and RNG states.

Null means unavailable. These are training-prefix diagnostics, not host validation. Four-category macro results and global Holm adjustment remain unavailable locally. Training trajectories, semantic donor compatibility, hidden labels, unavailable metadata, and simulator traits are unassessed. Patching cannot establish repair or validation gains.
